SMTO-CTX-0015 — SMTO asked for a part of an attached file that doesn't exist

GUID: 5a51f2fe-fbe0-4dc8-b0ab-da62acae7c80
Slug: context-read-invalid-range
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • While reading a file you attached, SMTO asked to start past the end of the file or asked for zero or fewer letters. Nothing was read and the file is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going for a step or two. SMTO sees this message and usually asks again with a valid starting point and amount.
  2. If it repeats, tell SMTO in the conversation: "Read the attached file again from the beginning." The beginning of the file is always a valid starting point.
  3. If SMTO keeps asking for a bad amount, open Agent Checks in the message box and, under Context & Attachments, turn on Read full attached context. With full reading on, SMTO ignores the amount it asked for and reads the rest of the file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps show text from the attached file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or re-attach the file; it isn't the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A read_context call supplied a negative or non-integer offset, an offset beyond the source's byte length, or a non-positive max_characters or limit amount (invalid_range).

What this means

  • Read positions must be nonnegative and within source bytes, while supplied bounded read amounts must be positive integers. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • Read positions must be nonnegative and within source bytes, while supplied bounded read amounts must be positive integers.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare offset with source byte length and verify the requested amount's type and positivity; distinguish an out-of-range position from an invalid page size.

How to fix it

  • Pass a nonnegative integer offset no larger than the source size and positive integer amounts, or continue with next_cursor (native/context_reads.py read_source).
  • Correct the offset and read amount within the source and captured policy bounds.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The same source accepts the corrected offset and positive supported amount.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
